H1.theory: Embedded SiC spheres scatter phonons via both mass and stiffness contrast plus interface strain; at 2 nm, MD with Tersoff gives a reduction within the continuum bracket because short-wavelength phonons are already alloy-scattered, so only mid-frequency phonons are removed.
H1.falsifier: An R = 2 nm run showing less than 35% or more than 78% reduction relative to the same alloy at equal composition.
H1.reach: If it holds, the continuum bracket can be used as a cold-start prior for nanoparticle effects in other SiGe-based transfer tasks.

H1b.theory: The Ge-free Si-rich shell removes alloy disorder scattering in a region around the particle, so the shell conducts better than the alloy, partly offsetting the particle; net effect depends on the volume fraction, but the shell's high-kappa Si-like region is large relative to the particle.
H1b.falsifier: A run in which particle plus Si-rich shell conducts more than the bare Si0.8Ge0.2 alloy.
H1b.reach: The control design for particle effects must separate the shell from the particle, changing how the H1 reduction is attributed.

H2.theory: Near pure Ge, alloy scattering vanishes and Tersoff-MD kappa rises steeply toward the pure-Ge value (finite-size-limited), which the quadratic-in-x resistivity law cannot capture; the high points are physical, a dilute-limit Nordheim divergence.
H2.falsifier: Repeated runs at x = 0.97 with different seeds and larger boxes giving kappa near 5 W/mK, on the law.
H2.reach: The outlier detector's fault flags in the high-Ge range should be reclassified as physics, and the law needs a dilute-limit term.

H3.theory: Virtual-crystal alloy kappa is a skewed U shape: Ge-rich side rises faster as Ge is heavier and alloy mass-disorder scattering scales as x(1-x); the interpolation between x=0.5 (4.30) and 0.85 (6.21) at 1100 K gives about 5.0 at 0.7.
H3.falsifier: almaBTE at x = 0.3 or 0.7 giving a lower kappa than at x = 0.5 at 1100 K.
H3.reach: The composition of minimum kappa informs where MD and literature are compared and the symbolic law's quadratic coefficient.

H4.theory: In an amorphous solid heat is carried by diffusons with short mean free paths, so kappa is length-independent apart from a weak propagon contribution at low frequency.
H4.falsifier: A kappa ratio above 1.4 between 96 and 24 cells in the amorphous box.
H4.reach: If it holds, amorphous values need no size extrapolation, unlike the crystalline MD values.

H5.theory: Tersoff-1989 overestimates Si phonon frequencies and has reduced anharmonicity, so GPUMD kappa at 300 K is above the DFT value; at 1100 K both converge toward Umklapp-limited values and agree more closely.
H5.falsifier: Tersoff at 1100 K more than 30% off the almaBTE 40.5 W/mK.
H5.reach: The MD-to-DFT fidelity offset for pure Si calibrates how much MD alloy values should be rescaled.

H6.theory: SiC formation is strongly favoured thermodynamically relative to substitutional C in a SiGe lattice, because of the large strain of a small C atom. C prefers Si neighbours over Ge by about 0.2 eV.
H6.falsifier: A MACE-MP-0 calculation giving substitutional C lower in energy than SiC.
H6.reach: The viability of carbon-doped SiGe as a precipitate-based thermal strategy and the choice of Si-rich shell in controls.

H7.theory: Biaxial compression changes bond stiffness and lifts cross-plane kappa slightly through the Grüneisen effect, while in-plane kappa falls modestly; for an alloy dominated by disorder scattering the net cross-plane effect is small.
H7.falsifier: A cross-plane change exceeding 10% in magnitude at 300 K.
H7.reach: Strain engineering would then not be a strong lever for kappa in SiGe films.

H8.theory: Sintered samples contain grain boundaries and porosity which lower kappa below the perfect virtual crystal; however, the virtual crystal overestimates the alloy scattering, so the ratio is moderate.
H8.falsifier: A median sintered-to-almaBTE ratio below 0.65 or above 1.0 from Starrydata2.
H8.reach: The database-versus-theory offset recalibrates how much weight literature values get relative to almaBTE.

H9.theory: Sn out-diffusion and segregation to the surface is driven by the free surface; the SiO2 cap removes the free surface and suppresses Sn surface segregation, so the change is suppressed.
H9.falsifier: Capped and uncapped films showing the same ellipsometry change at the same time at 550 C.
H9.reach: The role of surface versus bulk vacancy-mediated diffusion in the O1 and O2 questions.

O1.theory: Sn is large and strains the Ge lattice, so a neighbouring vacancy relieves strain and binds the Sn; a binding of about 0.3-0.5 eV is typical for DFT.
O1.falsifier: A MACE-MP-0 static calculation giving a binding energy below 0.15 eV.
O1.reach: Vacancy-assisted Sn mobility explains the low activation energy seen in annealing data.

O2.theory: Vacancy-mediated Sn hops in the MACE-MP-0 MD, with a vacancy already present, show only the migration barrier and not the formation energy, so the effective activation energy is well below the bulk-diffusion value.
O2.falsifier: Arrhenius analysis of the hops between 500 and 700 K yielding about 3 eV.
O2.reach: If it holds, the low-temperature metastable-film activation energy reflects vacancy-supported diffusion.

O3.theory: The thermodynamic driver (strong C-Si bonding, strain relief) is robust across potentials, but MACE-MP-0 softens the potential energy surface, so newer models likely give a larger energy gain.
O3.category: sign holds, magnitude changes by more than 0.3 eV
O3.falsifier: The newer model giving substitutional C favoured over SiC.
O3.reach: Confidence in all MACE-based energetic conclusions in the campaign.
